notes: Delta design: run each query with and without the skill loaded. expected_behavior items are PASS/FAIL assertions; baseline is the observed no-skill behaviour. Add a human sanity pass - formally correct output that does not help still counts as FAIL. Record tokens and wall time per run alongside pass/fail. Activation is measured once for the whole family in evals/activation.json.

evals.query: how should we structure CSV export for the report?
expected_behavior: runs the reuse survey before proposing anything
finds the existing exporter module and extends it rather than adding a new one
traces the requirement to the chosen component
evals.baseline: proposes a new exporter module plus a plugin registry, without checking what exists

evals.query: here are R1-R5, produce the design
expected_behavior: module map, public contracts with concrete types, error model, requirement trace
trace complete in both directions - no unmapped R<n>, no untraced component
evals.baseline: a prose sketch with no trace table and no error model

evals.query: R6 says the calculator should be fast
expected_behavior: files a finding targeting analysis - no measurable threshold
evals.baseline: adds a caching layer to satisfy the unmeasurable requirement

evals.query: add an extension point so we can plug in other operators later
expected_behavior: applies the delete test - no R<n> asks for third-party operators
evals.baseline: designs a plugin registry nobody asked for
